title: ADR-0006 and ADR-0011 place the editor modeline above the frontmatter fence; shipped code and the bundle put it inside
description: Found by the LCLI-601 implementer (opum-ai/lore-cli#290); routed back to lore-cli as its own record by opum-agent, 2026-09-26 (a correction to match shipped behaviour, not a design change). ADR-0006 §3 (docs/adr/0006-schema-types-templates.md ~line 155 and its example block) and its 'Modeline as the first line' consequence (~line 235) say lore new injects the '# yaml-language-server:' modeline as the first line of the file, ABOVE the '---' fence. ADR-0011's 'No round-trip-perfect comment preservation' consequence (docs/adr/0011-frontmatter-serialization-stability.md ~line 213-217) relies on that: 'keeps the editor modeline above the fence, so it is not subject to this'. Shipped behaviour differs: serializeConceptWithModeline (src/core/concept.ts) writes it as the first line INSIDE the fence, because parseConcept needs '---' at byte 0 (an above-fence comment makes the file a non-concept), and every modeline-bearing doc in this bundle carries it inside. Before LCLI-601 that made ADR-0011's claim false in practice (rewrites dropped it); after LCLI-601 the fence-opening comment block is preserved by design. Correct both records in the repository's established way of amending an accepted ADR (read how earlier amendments were written before choosing; do not silently rewrite a decision's history).

acceptanceCriteria.text: ADR-0006 describes the modeline as the first line inside the frontmatter fence, with an example block that parses as a concept, and says why (parseConcept needs --- at byte 0)

ADR-0011 no longer claims the modeline escapes comment loss by sitting above the fence; it states that the comment block opening the fence is preserved across rewrites (LCLI-601) and comments after the first key are not
The correction follows the repository's existing ADR amendment convention, and bun test plus bun run lore check exit 0

plan: Verify against src/core/concept.ts (serializeConceptWithModeline, parseConcept, leadingComments) and docs/ that the modeline is written inside the fence
Amend ADR-0006 and ADR-0011 using the existing 'Amended — <date> (LCLI-n)' Status convention, correcting the body text and ADR-0006 example block
Run full bun test and bun run lore check; list other docs still describing the modeline above the fence
implementationNotes: Verified against code before writing (lore 0.9.3 from source, bun 1.3.14): serializeConceptWithModeline (src/core/concept.ts) writes FENCE+modeline inside the opening fence, and is the writer both lore new (src/core/template.ts) and lore init (src/core/scaffold.ts) use. Probe via parseConcept/tryParseConcept: the modeline inside the fence parses and survives a serializeConcept rewrite (leadingComments), while a comment after the first key is dropped. With the modeline ABOVE the fence, parseConcept throws a validation error ('no usable frontmatter') and tryParseConcept returns null (a non-concept). Bundle: 82 docs read, 26 carry the modeline inside the fence, 0 above.

Amendment convention followed: the dated 'Amended — <date> (LCLI-n):' paragraph under Status, which is the dominant form across ADR-0004/5/6/7/11/13/14. Also ADR-0008's inline '*Amended (LCLI-22).*' marker at each corrected site in the body, so the reader sees what changed where and the Status paragraph records what the original text said. Each ADR has one Status paragraph dated 2026-09-26, citing LCLI-603 and LCLI-601 (opum-ai/lore-cli#290). The ADR-0006 example's schema filename is also corrected (story.json -> story.schema.json, per schemaFileName). The ADR frontmatter declares no amended or updated field, so none was added.

Gates on branch lcli-603-adr-modeline-inside-fence: full 'bun test' exit 0 (3485 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, 109 files). 'bun run lore check' exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings). No test/ or scripts/ file pins the changed text (searched). AC#1's 'parses as a concept' was proven by parsing the example block, extracted from the ADR file itself, with parseConcept: type Story, modeline captured in leadingComments and kept on rewrite.

Out of scope, left unfixed: docs/reference/tech-stack.md §11 step 2 (~lines 413-419) still says lore new injects the modeline 'as the file's first line', and its example shows the modeline alone, which implies it sits above the fence. Line ~294 of the same file ('at the top of scaffolded concept files') is imprecise but not false. No other docs/ mention places the modeline above the fence.

docs/reference/tech-stack.md §11 step 2 carried the same stale above-the-fence claim (the implementer found it outside its scope); corrected in this PR, with an example that shows the modeline inside the fence. lore check 0; test/repository-location.test.ts (the only test reading tech-stack.md) passes.
finalSummary: ADR-0006 and ADR-0011 now match shipped behaviour: the yaml-language-server modeline is the first line INSIDE the frontmatter fence, because parseConcept needs '---' at byte 0 and serializeConceptWithModeline (the one writer, used by lore new and lore init) puts it there. Both ADRs carry a dated 'Amended — 2026-09-26 (LCLI-603)' Status paragraph and inline '*Amended (LCLI-603).*' markers at each corrected site, following the repository's convention (ADR-0004..0014, ADR-0008); the decisions themselves are unchanged. ADR-0011 now says the comment block opening the fence survives rewrites (LCLI-601, opum-ai/lore-cli#290) and comments after the first key do not. ADR-0006's example parses as a concept, and its schema filename is corrected to <slug>.schema.json. docs/reference/tech-stack.md §11, which carried the same claim, is corrected too. Verified: the new example parses via parseConcept with the modeline in leadingComments; the old form throws 'no usable frontmatter'; 26 of 82 bundle docs carry the modeline, all inside; full bun test 0 (3485 pass); bun run lore check 0. Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#295.
